name: Dermatologist referral for bromhidrosis
lead: Bromhidrosis (osmidrosis) is foul-smelling body odor, often associated with excessive sweating that supports bacterial growth, especially in the underarms.[1] In looksmaxxing discussions, getting a medical evaluation is raised as a way to check for an underlying cause of persistent odor.

Body odor can signal disease, and related conditions include trimethylaminuria, a rare metabolic disorder causing a fishy odor in sweat, urine and breath.[1] Sources advise consulting a physician when odor affects quality of life.[1]

paras: Skin bacteria acting on apocrine sweat are the main source of odor, and diet, microbiome and genetics contribute.[1] Physicians may prescribe aluminum chloride antiperspirants; severe cases have been treated with endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy, which carries a risk of nerve injury.[1]

card.summary: Seeing a clinician to rule out medical causes of persistent body odor, such as hyperhidrosis or metabolic disorders.
card.note: Specific diagnostic pathways were not detailed in the sources reviewed.

quick.overview:
This entry covers getting a medical opinion for persistent body odor, rather than assuming it is hygiene-related.

Causes can include excessive sweating and, rarely, metabolic conditions such as trimethylaminuria.
quick.mechanism: A clinician can assess for hyperhidrosis or other conditions and may prescribe antiperspirants containing aluminum chloride.
quick.risks: Treatments for severe cases include surgery, which carries nerve-injury risk according to the sources reviewed.
